body:
**Chapter V10 - Secure Coding** 

Here are a few things I observed reviewing this chapter for v.5.0 for sanity check related to #2582: 

_V10.4 Defensive Coding_
Needs some paragraph describing this section. For consistency across all subsections in ASVS.

_V10.5 Security Architecture_
Needs some paragraph describing this section. For consistency across all subsections in ASVS.

Suggestion: 

`10.4.6 [ADDED] Verify that the application is able to discern and utilizes the user's true IP address to provide for sensitive functions, including rate limiting and logging.` 

This requirement doesn't feel like it should belong here in this chapter though. We may need to check out where else it could fit. Seems odd for it to be here.

comments.body:
> This requirement doesn't feel like it should belong here 

Can you explain, why it does not fit? Also see https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1389

Hey @csfreak92 I added section descriptions for 10.4 and 10.5 here can you take a look?

https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/pull/2613

I am trying to keep these brief, if you want them more verbose let me know.

> Can you explain, why it does not fit? Also see [#1389](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1389)

Because it seems that it does belong more in section V7.2 Security Events as the closest among every part of the other chapters, particularly on this phrase, `"application is able to discern and utilizes the user's true IP address"` of requirement 10.4.6.

> I am trying to keep these brief, if you want them more verbose let me know.

Fantastic descriptions @jmanico! I concur with those same as with Josh.

"Seems and feels" should be converted to arguments :)

I linked the issue where the discussion over category choice is discussed. the discussion over last change start from https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1389#issuecomment-2415895031

Correct IP is part of log event metadata, but it is not a security event itself.

The reason to have it in V10.4 - the application needs correct IP for everything - security decisions, to **produce** security events into logs, maybe for session management, geolocation. To watch "correct IP is only needed for (web server default) logs" is a bit oldschool.

So I think the requirement is in the correct place.

Ok, I can see now why it is under defensive coding. At first I was thinking that discerning and utilizing user's true IP address is part of detecting security events. Either we keep it here in V10.4 or move it to V7.2 I am good with it. 

Although, having the application `identify and perform security decisions` does sound as a job for another application/appliance in your network that should be doing that - such as SIEM, WAF and other network security tools, isn't it?

> Although, having the application `identify and perform security decisions` does sound as a job for another application/appliance in your network that should be doing that - such as SIEM, WAF and other network security tools, isn't it? 

@csfreak92 what are you referring to there? I could not find a reference to the phrase "identify and perform security decisions".

> > Although, having the application `identify and perform security decisions` does sound as a job for another application/appliance in your network that should be doing that - such as SIEM, WAF and other network security tools, isn't it?
> 
> [@csfreak92](https://github.com/csfreak92) what are you referring to there? I could not find a reference to the phrase "identify and perform security decisions".

@tghosth, not verbatim but identifying real users and performing security decisions is what is implied by this requirement: 

`10.4.6 [ADDED] Verify that the application is able to discern and utilizes the user's true IP address to provide for sensitive functions, including rate limiting and logging.` 

Isn't that what it is trying to say? Or did I get it wrong?

So in this case, I think the application may perform security decisions related to rate limiting (or it might outsource to another component) and it will certainly want the real IP address for logging.
Ah I see. Sounds good. Closing this issue as I think that clarifies it.
